score.note: First pass. The family matcher's template (main:080ce85c, member_orbit/run.c, score 7866/10000) is structurally related -- same 0x03001eec 'battle work' prologue idiom, same DrawRectangleFn/M2C_FIELD conventions -- but this owner (1192 bytes) is a genuinely different sub-effect from the template (724 bytes): a per-member burst of falling 'star' particles, not an orbiting ring. Drafted directly from games/gs1/asm/080da6cc.s and out/family-transplants/main-080da6cc/m2c/target.canonical.s (an m2c decompile of this owner's own retained bytes, not the template's), cross-checked instruction-by-instruction against the raw retained assembly rather than trusting m2c's output verbatim -- m2c mis-modeled both `bl Func_080072f4` call sites (the r4 slot of the _call_via_rN trampoline, already established family-wide: see games/gs1/recon/en/main/080dc1ec.json's score.note) as a fictional direct function with unresolved stack args, and silently dropped the width/height stack arguments and the (frame<threshold)?kind47:kind46 callback-selection logic entirely; both were reconstructed by hand-tracing the raw Thumb bytes (register-by-register) instead. Iterated with candidate-show --align through several genuine structural fixes, each independently verified to drop the score: (1) reordering the prologue's facing/extra_target reads to match the reference's actual read order (heap_cache-108 before heap_cache[2]), which also fixed `work`'s register from a stray fp allocation onto the reference's r9 for the whole function; (2) a real indexing bug -- `Data_080ede48[size2-2]` (auto-scaled by 2, giving byte offset size*4-4) where the reference's actual byte offset is size*2-2, i.e. plain `Data_080ede48[size-1]` (matching the established `Data_080ede48[idx-1]` idiom from games/gs1/recon/en/main/080dc1ec.c); (3) a real signedness bug -- `Data_080eea44[idx] >> 1` (the small-glint width halving) compiled to an arithmetic shift when the local was `s32`, but the reference emits a logical shift, so the source must genuinely be unsigned (fixed by declaring that local `u32`); (4) removing three inappropriately-cached locals (`count`/`raw_count`/`variant` used as the two idx-loops' *bound*) -- the reference recomputes `Data_080eea41[M2C_FIELD(M2C_FIELD(work,void**,0x7828),s32*,0x18)]` fresh at every loop-condition site (bumped matched_prefix 11->19 and dropped wrong_instructions 290->272 in one step, the single largest win of the pass); (5) inlining the burst-draw's callback ternary as raw byte-pointer arithmetic (`*(void**)((u8*)rectangle_slot+slot)` with slot=4-or-0) instead of `rectangle_slot[1]:rectangle_slot[0]`, which stopped the compiler from duplicating the entire call's argument setup into two branches; (6) introducing a named `size2` local so `size*2` is computed once and reused for both the table index and the height argument, instead of twice. Net over the pass: differing_halfwords 561->540, wrong_instructions 408->264, matched_prefix 11->19, candidate_bytes 1148->1168 (closer to the reference's 1192). Not exact. Residual (confirmed, not chased further): a single global register-role swap -- the reference keeps the outer idx-loop counter in sl and the cached &work[0x7828] address in fp for the entire burst/homing section; this candidate's compiler swaps them (idx in fp, the address in sl). This is exactly the family's documented 'loop-invariant address kept in a different high register than the reference' residual (see the task's own hard constraints and 080e01e4.json's open question (b)); every M2C_FIELD(work,void**,0x7828) site in this draft is written fresh at point of use (never hoisted into a named local) specifically so the compiler's own CSE decides the caching, per project convention, so this is not source-shape-controllable without forcing register assignment, which is prohibited. A smaller, separate residual: `rectangle[0] = *(void**)(Data_03001e50+46*4)` compiles to a folded pool literal + `ldmia` (4 bytes) where the reference does a fresh symbol load + two `adds` + `ldr` (8 bytes, presumably because the same 0x03001e50-based literal is reused nearby for the kind-47 fetch, +188, forcing the compiler to keep the bare symbol address live in a register rather than folding the offset into the pool word); tried an explicit `u32 *cache` cursor variable (matching puff_arc/run.c's proven-exact `cache=(u32*)(Data_03001e50+39*4); entry=cache; a=*entry++; b=*entry;` idiom) both with and without a call() between the two reads -- no effect either way, so this is recorded as open rather than forced. Two dead-code-shaped comparisons are deliberately preserved as literal source, matching the project's established 'record dead cells honestly' convention (see this session's 0801e318 work): `(Data_080eea41[variant] >> 1) != -132` guards the whole per-frame loop and is structurally unreachable-as-false (an unsigned 0-127 value can never equal -132), yet the reference's own compiler does not fold it away (confirmed: candidate-show --asm shows the identical `movs r5,#132; negs r5,r5; cmp r3,r5; bne/b` sequence verbatim once written as a literal -132 comparison, so the approved compiler genuinely does not perform this range-based fold and the reference's C likely wrote the same literal).

rejected_experiments: Modeled the Func_080072f4 call sites as m2c originally rendered them (a fictional direct 4-argument function with an unresolved 5th 'stack arg'): compiles, but drops the width/height arguments and the callback-selection entirely, and cannot reproduce the reference's r4-trampoline call shape at all. Cached the per-frame effect-state pointer (`M2C_FIELD(work, void**, 0x7828)`) into a single named `target` local, reassigned fresh before each use (matching games/gs1/recon/en/main/080d82b0.c's style): this is exactly the pattern the task's own guidance warns against (a materialized derived pointer inviting CSE-driven hoisting/spill); switched to writing the nested M2C_FIELD expression fresh at every single use site instead (no named local at all), which is what let the compiler's own register allocator decide caching -- and is very likely why it independently chose to keep the address live in a high register (fp in this draft, sl in the reference) for the busy burst/homing section, matching the reference's overall shape even though the specific register differs.

Cached the two idx-loops' iteration bound (`Data_080eea41[variant]`) into a named `count`/`raw_count` local computed once before each do-while: the reference recomputes this expression fresh at the loop-condition site every iteration (confirmed via the raw bytes: `mov r1,fp; ldr r3,[r1,#0]; ldr r3,[r3,#24]; ldrb r3,[r2,r3]; cmp sl,r3` appears at the tail of both loops, not a cached stack read). Removing the cached locals and writing the fresh nested expression at both the entry-gate and the loop-condition was the single largest win of this pass (wrong_instructions 290->272, matched_prefix 11->19).

Wrote the burst-draw's callback selection as a ternary directly in the DrawRectangleFn call position, `(frame<threshold)?rectangle_slot[1]:rectangle_slot[0]`: the compiler duplicated the entire remaining call-argument setup into two branches instead of the reference's flag-then-single-indexed-load shape. Rewrote as an explicit `slot=(frame<half_idx+48)?4:0;` local plus a single raw byte-pointer dereference `*(void**)((u8*)rectangle_slot+slot)`, matching the reference's actual `mov ip,#4/#0; ldr r4,[r5,r0]` register-offset addressing and collapsing back to one call site.

Left a shared `threshold2 = half_idx+48;` local reused at both the callback-selection site and the later homing gate: the reference recomputes `half_idx+48` fresh at each site (two separate `adds r7,#48` sequences, not one cached value carried across the intervening burst-draw body). Removed the shared local; both sites now write `half_idx + 48` as their own fresh expression.

Declared `Data_080eea44[idx]`'s halving result as `s32 w = Data_080eea44[idx]; x = cur->x - (w>>1);`: compiles to an arithmetic shift (asrs) since the local is signed, but the reference emits a logical shift (lsrs). Retyped the local `u32`, which fixed the shift and, as a side effect, corrected the surrounding instruction ordering to match the reference (the u16 source-table read now happens at the same point in the instruction stream as the reference instead of being deferred to just before the call).

Semantic summary: a per-member 'falling star' battle-presentation sub-effect. Seeds 64 Star records (x,y,z,vx,vy,vz,state; 28 bytes, at 0x02010000) once from a single member's screen position with randomized velocities (state=-1, meaning 'not yet released'). Runs `(Data_080eea41[variant]>>1)+132` animation frames, where `variant` is a small (0..2) field read from the caller's effect-state struct at offset 0x18. Each frame, a per-variant subset of the 64 stars (the raw count at Data_080eea41[variant], up to 64) is walked by index: once `idx/2` frames have elapsed, a still-released(-1) star draws a shrinking trail sprite through the kind-46/47 rectangle-blit callback cache (Data_03001e50[46]/[47]) -- kind 47 while still inside its own `idx/2 .. idx/2+48` window, kind 46 once 48 frames overdue -- sized from its own projected screen distance (Func_080e3944, clamped [160,799]), and its position drifts by its own velocity every such frame. Once 48 frames overdue, the same star is also 're-homed' every frame: its velocity is nudged 1/512 of the way toward its member's live screen position (Func_080b5098), damped to 60/64 strength for frames before `idx/2+85`, full strength after. Once a homed star's Y position crosses above the top of the screen (y<0), it 'lands': state flips to 0, its position snaps to the just-computed projected screen position, a sound cue and a Func_080d6888 dispatch fire at its member, and a work-block flag (offset 0x77A8) is set. Independently, every frame, a second full 64-star scan draws any star whose state is in [0,11] (i.e. just landed) through a fixed twelve-frame 'glint' sequence -- four small per-index tables (Data_080eea44 width, Data_080eea4a height, Data_080eea50 y-delta, Data_080eea56 source offset), always through the kind-47 callback -- incrementing state each frame until it exceeds 11 and the star goes dormant.

The `Data_080eea41`/`44`/`4a`/`50`/`56` tables are new to the tracked corpus (no prior owner references these addresses); their extents were inferred from the reference's own index math (variant in 0..2 for the 3-byte count table; state/2 in 0..5 for the four 6-entry small tables) rather than known table lengths, and are recorded here as u8/u16 arrays with no further symbolic name pending a second owner that shares them.

Callee signatures for Func_080b5070, Func_080b5028, Func_080f9010, Func_080e155c and Func_080b50e8 follow the already-established prototypes from games/gs1/recon/en/main/080d82b0.c, 080d1350.c and 080c91dc.c (all plain s32-argument functions); Func_080022fc's `s32(s32,s32)` prototype and Func_080b5098's `void**(s32)` prototype follow member_orbit/run.c and 080d82b0.c respectively.

The Func_080e0524 id arguments use the established `(s32)&Value_XXXXXXXX` pool-literal idiom (Value_000000b4 already adopted in puff_arc/run.c; Value_00000073 already adopted in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080e01e4.c) rather than plain int literals, matching the family-wide finding that this callee's id argument is always pool-loaded. Func_080ed408's id arguments (46/47) and the tail Func_08002dd8(46/47) calls are plain int literals, matching member_orbit/run.c and puff_arc/run.c exactly -- confirmed from the raw bytes (`movs r0,#46` / `movs r0,#47`, never a pool load) for every occurrence in this owner.
